Params: The high-speed elevator plunges at full tilt, enough to make your spine go numb.
Adelyde holds you firmly in the corner of the lift, shielding you from the impact and carefully checking on you.
I've done far worse than this.
I... I just need a moment.
At least the elevator still works.

After we repaired Ananke and completed the evacuation three decades ago, the Atlantic Eye's spacetime was frozen at the moment just before the calamity. The facilities were restored, but no one could enter or use them.

Before anyone on the outside could figure out how to break this spacetime lock, the Punishing Virus broke out soon after. No one had the time to worry about a giant frozen relic, and the TEC never recovered.

The Helio family had the ending right, but they thought their greatest threat was zero-point energy and space colonization, when it was the Punishing Virus that tore apart their global infrastructure and energy industry.
Those who dissolved into the Consciousness Tide...
A flicker of buried pain flashes across Adelyde's face.
None of them made it back.
The chime of arrival snaps you both to attention. Adelyde rises and pulls you up from the floor.
Just then, a piercing shriek erupts from beyond the elevator doors. Both of you activate your weapons immediately.
Expect a wide mix of hostiles. We might encounter Red Tide Hetero-Creatures, Corrupted, and Atlantic Eye security mechs that have gone out of control. Be ready to adapt.
She glances back at you, her voice as steady as it was all those years ago when she ran you through a plan before a simulation drill.
Clear the immediate threat first. Once we're in the clear, survey the terrain and reconfirm the objective.
The elevator doors slide open. Before you can even count the enemies ahead, a terrifying beam is fired from Adelyde's cannon.
Every twisted creature in the beam's path vaporizes instantly. Even their own kind hesitate, faltering briefly.
Adelyde runs a hand along the barrel and whispers.
It's the same one from before. It's one of the few pieces of the past I took with me when I left Helio.
Glory, disappointment, regret... Everything from those years that I couldn't speak of and couldn't forget has been forged into this cannon.
This... is what I've been waiting for!
The glint of crosshairs flares in Adelyde's eyes, and she swings her cross cannon forward and charges. You rush to keep up, gun raised to cover her flank.
The red-clad Construct is nothing short of awe-inspiring when she is not holding back. Precision and raw power, two qualities that rarely coexist, are both on full display in this fight.

Your gaze drifts to Adelyde's right arm, which has transformed into a machine gun. Noticing how every part of her frame is built for battle, you catch a glimpse of all the years she spent wading through blood.
Not a single attack from the front or the flanks gets past her. Her coverage is airtight, and you are free to observe the state of the Atlantic Eye as you push forward.
There's an intact Ananke sub-unit over there. Let's push in that direction.
Spent casings clatter across the floor. Adelyde sweeps the area, making sure that all hostiles are down before retracting her gun.
Her gaze turns to the dismembered limbs of the Hetero-Creature scattered across the dark, slick floor. She frowns.
Before we came in, there was one thing I couldn't figure out... Where exactly was the Red Tide flooding out of the Atlantic Eye coming from?
After spending so long inside Ananke, I think I have a theory.
She points to where the rays from the Ananke sub-units terminate. The Red Tide is lying in wait at the end of the golden threads.

At its core, Ananke is a transmission channel for data structures across spacetime. Matter, energy, and information can all pass through it... and the Punishing Virus is a kind of data structure itself.
So the Red Tide has likely been hunting us through Ananke from the other dimensions it connects to.
But there was no Red Tide flooding out before the moon rock strike.
Exactly. Which leads to the conclusion that the Red Tide flooding out of the Atlantic Eye is a direct result of Ananke being damaged.

If Ananke is a pipe, the Consciousness Tide energy is the clean water running through it, and the Punishing Virus is the contamination outside. A cracked pipe doesn't just leak clean water. It also lets the contamination seep in.
If we repair Ananke, we can seal off both in one go.
The two of us certainly got the hands-on experience for it.
Second time's the charm, I suppose.
Once Ananke is repaired, your administrative access should let you extract the half of the "Understanding" Sefirah it's locked away.
With that, the Sefirah, the surges, and the Red Tide... all three of our objectives will be taken care of.
We still can't confirm the whereabouts of Arius and Rusalka.
Arius said he'd be waiting for us at the Sefirah Engine, and that's most likely true.
The Sefirah has to be extracted... His entire scheme is an open play. He's too arrogant to even bother hiding his intentions from us.
Her eyes darken, and her hand curls into a fist.
And if Rusalka insists on throwing her life away for Arius, I don't mind knocking some sense into her first before reminiscing about the past.
The comms from every strike team that breached the Atlantic Eye light up at once, all patching into your terminal.
All teams, are you free to receive an update from us?
Sounds of combat still crackle through the comms, but Lucia answers almost immediately.
The sounds of the pyro katana's strikes die down, and Lee joins the comms.
We're clear for now. How about you guys?
Status reports come in one after another. Once Adelyde finishes tallying them, she switches the comms to a one-way broadcast, then signals you to begin.
The key to this operation is repairing and restarting Ananke.
It's the same approach as what was done during the Atlantic Calamity.
Step one: follow your detectors' guide to locate and reactivate all the Ananke sub-units scattered throughout the area, and establish Ananke's Link.
Step two: the connection will point us to the location of Ananke's main control room, where the reconstruction key needs to be entered manually.
Step three: the moment Ananke is reconstructed, Sefirah needs to be extracted from the Sefirah Engine at the lowest level of the dam.
All three steps have to move forward at the same time, so we'll need to split up.
Lucia, Lee, find the control room. Others, the sub-units. We'll get the engine.
Scientists from both sides risked charges of treason to build the Atlas Shield together, and that's the only reason we could enter the Atlantic Eye safely and face Arius on even ground.
Now, we're ordering everyone to scatter from their teammates in unfamiliar territory and march into unknown danger.
The image of a figure in white aboard a transport craft pressing a badge so hard into her palm it drew blood decades ago overlaps with the figure in red standing here now.
Aristo spoke of love and pride, but I'll tell you the part he left out... The people who achieved that miracle during the Atlantic Calamity chose to connect out of despair and defiance.
Their ideals were already shattered. All they could do was slow the gears of fate and buy their people a little more time.
But that little time was enough to keep the spark of creation alive, enough to make peace and say goodbye.
Enough for us to catch up.
<color=#ffffffff><size=45>Is this chase exhausting? Do all those what-ifs and should-haves hurt? Do the endless fights feel frustrating?</size></color>
Is this chase exhausting? Do all those what-ifs and should-haves hurt? Do the endless fights feel frustrating?
<color=#ffffffff><size=45>It is exhausting. They do hurt. They do feel frustrating.</size></color>
It is exhausting. They do hurt. They do feel frustrating.
It was never just light and hope that kept everyone going.
And yet we made it here. We're still here.
This is our idealism: finding strength in despair and defiance, in everything we hate and everything we refuse to lose.
Only now do you realize that Adelyde has kept the two-way comms open between the Gray Ravens and you.
Lucia's voice is steady and calm. Her resolve radiates light and heat like a star, and you can feel it without a M.I.N.D. connection.
Were you worried that we wouldn't let you walk into danger, Commandant?
I don't even have to guess the expression on your face right now. It's that look that says, "I'm sorry, but I have to do this," right?
The Construct who has never quite known what to do with you is not really looking for your answer. He just sighs.
Then you already know that we'll give everything we have for you, no matter what happens and where in the world you need us.
I feel the same about you both.
So don't worry. We can do this, and so can you.
A torrent of conviction surges through your every bone and sinew, allowing your ordinary human body to rise and run forward once again.
You take a deep breath and stand straight. Turning around, you find Adelyde on the terminal with a warm and relieved smile.
You've found such wonderful companions along the way.
Drop by the Gray Raven Lounge whenever you have time.
She closes her eyes for a brief moment, then snaps back into focus.
The Sefirah Engine is at the lowest level of the Atlantic Eye. We must keep up with the other teams, so we need to take every shortcut allowed—hm?
Behind the Ananke sub-unit nearby, a small crystalline creature flinches at the sight of Adelyde's cannon, shrinking back in alarm.
How did one end up here... Oh. Right. We did release a batch during the relief efforts back then.
Surviving this long inside the Atlantic Eye... Quite impressive.
These ecological sponges were developed specifically for deep-sea operations to purify water and generate oxygen. They used to be everywhere inside the Atlantic Eye.
Adelyde narrows her eyes and studies it carefully, then pauses.
Its ears are a little shorter than the other Huhus.
The Huhu that snuck aboard the Kelpie and set sail with three girls, the one that Adelyde pulled to safety with her own hands during the Atlantic Calamity... is the one before her right now.
...So it's you. You actually made it. Good job.
Crouching down, she scoops the little creature up, lifts it to her eye level, then speaks slowly and deliberately.
The Sefirah Engine. Can you lead us there safely?
Those round eyes blink a few times before the creature lets out two soft cries of "huhu!"
